searchText: The most common reason for a 1 slot reorg on mainnet is that the proposer was not well connected to the next proposer and the latter didn't see the block in time. In this situation one of the two blocks will necessarily be orphaned Interesting thanks. You’d think there would be enough time. It’s less than a seconds delay to get data from western USA to India. It's not only network lag, there's also bad peering, some people are staking on raspberry pi that may be overwhelmed at the time, and a number of other factors Ah I see. I assume it’ll get better on mainnet assuming most validation is coming from central servers in datacentres. I guess they also get punished for not propagating their block well so there’s incentives to do a good job. We used blox routes endpoints to propagate blocks on pow and it works really well helped reduce uncles a lot. They don't. In fact there's an economic incentive in sending their block as late as possible. Lighthouse is the only team that has been aggressively trying to target this and fork late blocks off. If this becomes a real problem I think all teams will implement a similar algorithm I get that in terms of loading up the fattest block possible and doing more mev but don’t you risk losing out entirely if the chain skips it? Yeah but paraphrasing someone here: if there's a threshold to be measured, these people will try it Thanks I understand the issues now i've got the block root on an archive node, if you did need that block.. That would be great, please could you drop me a link to it? https://github.com/rolfyone/playground/raw/main/goerli/3692574.json.gz Thanks, the parent root of that block is non-canonical as well, so suspect that the proposer was off in its own little world. i ended up having to get headers for that slot then fetch by root, but at least its accessible i guess 🙂 parent slot was 3692543, built on 542, and 542 was canonical so the non canonical block it built on was definitely in its own little world FYI: this script is very helpful in grabbing a chain of potentially non-canonical blocks: https://www.symphonious.net/2022/08/18/beacon-rest-api-fetching-blocks-on-a-fork/ There was a recent post about Goerli reorgs in the <#892088344438255616> channel https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/892088344438255616/1009669936366493696 I think this statement is correct if the network is 100% synchronous up to 4s which is unreachable in practice. This is actually the idea behind safe block algorithm. But even on the mainnet participation rate isn't 100% which reflects either asynchrony or other issue with different validators, there are missed slots too which pushes us further from this theoretical statement. On testnets with much lower participation rates (which I am using now as an indicator of various issues) than on the mainnet situations with reorg is even worse. Mainnet post-Merge should be much more stable in that regard I raised this https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/issues/231 as temp-checker and place for additional conversation https://nimbus.guide/el-light-client.html - nimbus light client mentioned on consensus call - can drive an execution client using the light client protocol Notes from the consensus devs call: https://hackmd.io/@benjaminion/Hy_d7lryj in that issue it was mentioned to raise a PR... https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/232

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: The most common reason for a 1 slot reorg on mainnet is that the proposer was not well connected to the next proposer and the latter didn't see the block in time. In this situation one of the two blocks will necessarily be orphaned

excerpts.author: chris2_2_2
excerpts.content: Interesting thanks. You’d think there would be enough time. It’s less than a seconds delay to get data from western USA to India.

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: It's not only network lag, there's also bad peering, some people are staking on raspberry pi that may be overwhelmed at the time, and a number of other factors

excerpts.author: chris2_2_2
excerpts.content:
Ah I see. I assume it’ll get better on mainnet assuming most validation is coming from central servers in datacentres.

I guess they also get punished for not propagating their block well so there’s incentives to do a good job.

excerpts.author: chris2_2_2
excerpts.content: We used blox routes endpoints to propagate blocks on pow and it works really well helped reduce uncles a lot.

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: They don't. In fact there's an economic incentive in sending their block as late as possible. Lighthouse is the only team that has been aggressively trying to target this and fork late blocks off. If this becomes a real problem I think all teams will implement a similar algorithm

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
I think this statement is correct if the network is 100% synchronous up to 4s which is unreachable in practice. This is actually the idea behind safe block algorithm. But even on the mainnet participation rate isn't 100% which reflects either asynchrony or other issue with different validators, there are missed slots too which pushes us further from this theoretical statement.

On testnets with much lower participation rates (which I am using now as an indicator of various issues) than on the mainnet situations with reorg is even worse. Mainnet post-Merge should be much more stable in that regard
